name: Michael Burry
detail: Known for anticipating the U.S. housing collapse. A complete, comparable 2016–2025 net-return record has not been verified for this arena. Quarterly holdings cannot reconstruct his full strategy, including shorts and derivatives.

name: Ray Dalio
detail: Founder of Bridgewater and author of Principles. Any comparison must identify the particular fund, its risk target and Dalio’s management period. Bridgewater’s later results should not automatically be attributed to its founder.

name: Jim Cramer
detail: CNBC’s investing personality and the public face of its Charitable Trust. A continuous return history and its cash-flow treatment still need verification. The trust’s results and the performance of every stock mentioned on television are different things.

name: Peter Lynch
detail: Managed Fidelity Magellan from 1977 to 1990. His comparison belongs to that management period, using the S&P 500 total-return index because SPY launched later. Today’s Magellan returns would measure other managers, so he has no 2016–2025 rank.

name: Charlie Munger
detail: A central figure in Berkshire’s history. His independent partnership and his work at Berkshire need separate attribution and historical periods. The arena does not duplicate Buffett’s Berkshire result as an independent Munger track record.

name: George Soros
detail: Founder associated with the Quantum Fund and global macro investing. A historical comparison needs a verified fund series and the years of his direct involvement. Current family-office holdings are not his personal investment return.

name: Kevin O’Leary
detail: Recognizable from Shark Tank and associated with O’Shares. OUSA has a public fund record dating to 2015, which still needs to be added and checked here. It tracks an index: its results would represent an associated fund, not O’Leary’s personal portfolio or his Shark Tank investments.

name: Ken Griffin
detail: Founder of Citadel. A return comparison needs a named fund, a consistent net-of-fees series and recognition of the firm’s investment teams. Citadel Securities is a separate business, and reported securities holdings are not fund performance.

name: Stanley Druckenmiller
detail: Founded Duquesne Capital and previously managed the Quantum Fund. Duquesne Capital closed to outside investors in 2010. A historical track record needs its own dates; later family-office filings do not establish a full 2016–2025 net return.

name: Jim Simons
detail: Founder of Renaissance Technologies. Medallion and Renaissance’s external funds have different records and access. Any historical comparison must identify the exact fund and fee basis; a reported headline return is not enough to assign a ten-year rank.

name: Howard Marks
detail: Oaktree co-founder and author of widely read investment memos. Oaktree manages multiple strategies, including credit. A comparison needs a specific fund and matching return measure; private-fund IRRs cannot be treated as an equity fund’s annualized total return.

name: Paul Tudor Jones
detail: Founder of the Tudor Group. The firm runs multiple investment strategies. A full ten-year net-return series for a named vehicle still needs verification before this profile can enter the numerical leaderboard.

name: David Einhorn
detail: Founder of Greenlight Capital. Investor letters provide a starting point, but a consistent 2016–2025 series still needs to be assembled and checked. Greenlight’s hedge-fund return and Greenlight Capital Re’s share-price return are different records.

name: Ron Baron
detail: Founder of Baron Capital and a portfolio manager of Baron Partners alongside Michael Baron. Public fund returns are available; the annual series still needs to be added and checked here. Its concentrated portfolio, leverage and private-company valuations must remain visible in the comparison.

name: Dan Loeb
detail: Founder of Third Point. This record follows the Offshore Fund, including legacy private investments, after reported fund fees and expenses. Its mix of equities, credit and hedges differs from SPY. Reported fee conventions changed in 2020; it is a fund record, not Loeb’s personal return.

name: Mohnish Pabrai
detail: The comparison uses Pabrai Investment Fund 3 consistently, not a blend of the best-performing Pabrai funds. Annual net returns in Appendix B are checked against year-end NAVs in Appendix D of the 2025 annual report. The ten-year result is calculated from those observations because the report’s headline summary table is inconsistent with its appendices.
sourceLabel: Pabrai · annual reports and NAV history

name: Terry Smith
detail: Fundsmith Equity T Accumulation total returns, after fund expenses, translated from GBP into USD at each year-end. Currency movements are included. This global-equity strategy has a different investment universe from the S&P 500; SPY measures the alternative of buying the U.S. index.

name: Mario Gabelli
detail: Gabelli Asset Fund Class AAA (GABAX) total returns, with distributions reinvested and fund expenses included. Class AAA has no sales load. Gabelli leads a management team; these are the fund’s results rather than his personal portfolio or GAMCO’s share price.

name: Will Danoff
detail: Fidelity Contrafund (FCNTX) NAV total returns, after fund expenses, with distributions reinvested. Danoff managed the fund throughout this comparison period. Asher Anolic and Jason Weiner joined him as co-managers in April 2025, so the final year includes a shared management team.

name: Cliff Asness
detail: AQR Long-Short Equity Fund Class I (QLEIX), co-managed by Asness and the AQR team. Published NAV returns include fund expenses and reinvested distributions. The strategy targets moderate equity exposure and uses short positions; beating SPY is an opportunity-cost comparison, not its stated mandate.

name: Bruce Berkowitz
detail: The Fairholme Fund (FAIRX), led by Bruce Berkowitz, measured at NAV after expenses with distributions reinvested. Its concentrated holdings can produce large differences from the broad S&P 500. The record covers calendar years 2016–2025, rather than the fund’s November fiscal-year endpoints.

name: Prem Watsa
detail: Fairfax Financial shareholder total returns, including dividends, translated into USD. This measures an investment in the listed company, including its insurance operations and valuation changes. It is not the return on Fairfax’s investment portfolio or Watsa’s personal wealth.

name: Tom Gayner
detail: Markel Group (MKL) shareholder return in USD. Gayner was co-CEO during 2016–2022 and CEO from 2023. The share return includes insurance and operating businesses, investment results, and market valuation; it is not the return of the equity portfolio he manages.

name: John Hussman
detail: Hussman Strategic Market Cycle Fund (HSGFX), formerly Strategic Growth, at NAV with distributions reinvested. Its mandate emphasizes capital protection and varying market exposure. Hedging can cause it to lag a rising equity market; the comparison with SPY measures opportunity cost, not whether it met its risk-management objective.

name: Bill Nygren
detail: Oakmark Fund Investor Class (OAKMX), after fund expenses with distributions reinvested. Bill Nygren was a manager throughout 2016–2025; the fund is co-managed. Its value-oriented portfolio can differ substantially from the S&P 500’s sector and style exposures.

name: Chris Davis
detail: Davis New York Venture Fund Class A (NYVTX), co-managed by Chris Davis and Danton Goei. NAV total returns include operating expenses and reinvested distributions but exclude the maximum 4.75% initial sales charge. An investor paying that charge would receive lower returns.

name: John Rogers Jr.
detail: Ariel Fund Investor Class (ARGFX) NAV total returns with distributions reinvested and expenses included. Rogers leads the management team. The fund focuses on small and mid-sized value stocks; SPY is an alternative investment comparison rather than its primary strategy benchmark.

name: David Herro
detail: Oakmark International Fund Investor Class (OAKIX), co-managed by David Herro, with expenses included and distributions reinvested. USD returns include the currency exposure of its international holdings. Its investment universe differs from U.S.-focused SPY.
